utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We held, by far, smaller territory than was the case with the Muslim side, and I think that the ratio was 30 to 70 per cent, meaning that the Bosnian Government held 70 per cent of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put number 1?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you now also circle these blue Serbian villages inside the Muslim territory?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Put the number 2 next to it.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me, what was the fate of these villages? Can you tell the Chamber what happened with the residents of the villages who remained behind?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, it was very bad. Mr. Karadzic, if you will allow me, I need some time, and I think it would be beneficial for you, but primarily I want to say this for the benefit of the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could be as concise as possible, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Yesterday, I spoke, among other things, about part of the Muslim population, especially able-bodied men, and I failed to mention a very important matter which will be of great assistance to the Trial Chamber, but also to the Prosecution, and that is as follows: When the indoctrination was taking place, it is very important to point out a feature that would later on, in the relationship between the Serbs and Bosniaks in that area, have a significant effect, and that is the following feature: In spite of the very difficult and complex situation, there were some areas where both Serbs and Muslims were very tolerant of each other. They did not want the war; they wanted peace. I can say this with a clear mind and with a lot of arguments because I know of these instances and cases. There were towns and villages where people actually stood guard together. But, unfortunately, after the SDA activities and the Crisis Staff from the Bosnian Corps in the area of Hadzici, Ilidza and Trnovo, and because they did not like this situation, they did all they could in order to upset the balance and the tolerance that existed, both in terms of the faith, the religion, and also the culture and customs of the ethnic groups that lived there, both Muslim and Serb. What I'm saying now, you can actually see for yourself. There are numerous documents collected by the security services, and everything that I've said here can be seen in numerous documents that were collected by the security services. The crisis staffs decided to bring into those areas KOS [as interpreted] members, K-O-S members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what HOS is?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. H-O-S.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the Croatian Defence Forces, but I have to say that all the members of HOS were members of Bosniak nationality who had already taken part in fighting in Croatia and who had already fought Serbs in those areas. Now they returned to this area and continued with the same activities that they had been involved in earlier on. They declared themselves, and we were very well aware of that, as haters of Serbs. They came to Hadzici and Hrasnica and also Sokolovic Kolonija, and also to the Trnovo area, and in a very brief time they managed to commit numerous war crimes and all kinds of other illicit activities which, as I've already said, were documented by the police. And I personally submitted a number of criminal reports against certain individuals, and these criminal reports were sent to the competent prosecutor's offices, some of them in Republika Srpska and the others in the Federation. Now, the reason I'm saying this is for the Trial Chamber, when trying to get the whole picture of the situation in the area, and that can then serve as a prototype for all other areas where the Serb population was in the minority, this is how things were actually carried out. And, gentlemen, everything I've said here can be found in a book published in 1996, written by Munir Alibabic, aka Munja. And let me just say that he was an old-type, very capable member of the former State Security Service who was the chief of the Centre of the Security Services of Sarajevo during the war. The title of the book was "Bosna in the cause of KOS," K-O-S, which is the Military Counter-Intelligence Service. This was a book by Mr. Munir Alibabic right after the war in 1996, and in it he talks about these groups of HOS members that I spoke about a little earlier, and he acknowledges and admits on one of the pages of this book that these men committed war crimes and that certain groups from Herzegovina committed war crimes. And as you read on in the book, you can actually deduce that he was referring to the HOS members. And what is also very important is to say is a witness testified about a crime committed in Trebevic [as interpreted], which is in Trnovo municipality, to the fact that members of HOS killed every living soul in that village, and when a member of Bosniak ethnicity asked the leader of the group, Why did you do this, why did you kill the elderly and the women? They literally said, Well, why did you call us up here? So I told you about this deliberately in order for you to get an overall picture of what the situation was like down there, where we were, when these people came back from other areas. When they came back to Pazarici and on their way back to Herzegovina, they stated, literally, We've managed to create such a deep rift between the Serbs and the Muslims that they will never again manage to live together in this area. And I just have to add that they were quite successful in what they set out to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I felt I had to rise, because I think we've come to a situation where this evidence has gone so far to the edge of being relevant that it actually has crossed the line into being tu quoque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is a Prosecution witness, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I asked him to be concise. But let's move on, Mr. Karadzic. Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, thank you for pointing these things out, but may I ask you now to be as brief as possible. Tell us, please, these Muslims from the green areas around Hadzici, did they go to the green areas and actually carry out the evacuation themselves?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about the Serbs in the blue Serb villages; were they allowed to cross over to Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way, out of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were they arrested, and were they detained at the silos camp, silos?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, almost all of them, and I'm referring to men, although there were also some female prisoners.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We will show a document, but before that I would like to do away with the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you just tell me now one more thing? When speaking about the establishment of two municipalities, did the Serbs have in mind the blue areas, and did they actually include these blue areas in their municipalities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's -- that's what it -- that's how it was, and I believe I said as much in my statement provided to the Prosecution. These were the Serb villages, and there were no pretensions on Muslim areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When people say that the -- when they said that they took over the municipalities, did the Serbs take control over the entire municipalities or just their own areas under the Serb -- or, rather, their part of the municipality? So is that how it transpired in Hadzici? Did they just take over the Serb parts?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please date and sign this map?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies, but what is the date.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it's the 15th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1064, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And that will be it for today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I just had one last question about this same area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Glavas, did your family have the same fate -- meet the same fate as the Serbs that were in the Muslim territory, Muslim-controlled territory?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my entire family, my two brothers, my father, and even my mother was supposed to be arrested, but I was tipped off by Croats and we managed to save her. Otherwise, I'm sure she would have been taken prisoner as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we briefly see 1D3242 in e-court. 1D3242, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it to appear on the screens, let me read out the content, and we can also -- we can see the English version. And it says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the date.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Based on intelligence from the ground, we've managed to learn the following." Why can't we have this document on the screen? Okay, now we have it. So we have the Serbian version. Could we show the English version? Oh, we don't have it. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, take a look at this. On the 19th of August, 1992 -- that's the date of this document. So it says there: "In the area of Tarcin, the Muslim forces are deployed at Metarica [phoen] ...," and so on. But let us see what it says further down in the third paragraph: "The situation at the silo is very difficult, and the leaders of the Serb population are the ones who are exposed to greatest levels of torture; Plakalovic, Vaso; Nenad Kostic, who armed Serbs; Mile Bratic, the staff commander; Laza Kostic, father of Dragan Krstic, who was declared a Chetnik duke; and Vlastimir Glavas, the brother of Tihomir Glavas, were the ones who were tortured most." So is that true? Is this your brother, and was he tortured there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR GLAVAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to admit this into evidence, and I would like to add something. I can do it in the presence of the witness, but perhaps it would be more appropriate, because of the Prosecution, to do it without the presence of this witness. Something to do with a comment by Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll mark it for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1065, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Glavas. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to say something that relates to what Ms. Edgerton said. I just want to say that the Defence does -- it is not the intention of the Defence to use the tu quoque principle. All we want is for the Trial Chamber to get a full picture of what went on there and how it went on, whether there was a plan in place, being put in place, or whether it was a civil war, whether there was a state plan for this, years before it happened, before this conflict broke out, whether the state leadership already had a plan for that or not. And this is what we are trying to show here, and not trying to actually use the tu quoque defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I indicated to you several times before, the criminal trial is not conducted for the purpose of creating or pre-producing a white book. Certainly, it is important to understand the context, but we don't have to go in detail. Bear that in mind. We rise. Tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of February, 2011, at 9:00 a.m.
